title: How to test langgraph Functional API entrypoints
q_body: In the official docs they only show how to test Graph API (StateGraph): https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/test#getting-started Our team is discussing alternatives to write such tests for the Functional API , especially regarding checkpointer injection. 1. Use builder to pass checkpointer To test entrypoints with InMemorySaver I decided to wrap each entrypoint function into a builder function like this: def wf1_builder(cp): @entrypoint(checkpointer=cp) async def wf1(...): ... return wf1 This way I can test them like this: async def test_wf1: wf1_test = wf1_builder(InMemorySaver()) result = await wf1_test.ainvoke(...) I think that this approach is analogous to the example tests that official docs show for Graph API. 2. Substitute checkpointer using copy If I define the entrypoint at 1st level, I could substitute the checkpointer e.g. with copy , although I don't like it because it looks like a hack. global_checkpointer = build_postgres_saver() @entrypoint(checkpointer=global_checkpointer) async def wf1(...): ... async def test_wf1: wf1_test = wf1.copy({ "checkpointer": InMemorySaver() }) result = await wf1_test.ainvoke(...) 3. Initialize checkpointer depending on environment By defining a different global checkpointer depending on environment (test/prod), both entrypoint definitions and tests look cleaner. Although I still don't like it, due to using global variables. if os.getenv("ENV") == "test": global_checkpointer = InMemorySaver() else: global_checkpointer = build_postgres_saver() @entrypoint(checkpointer=global_checkpointer) async def wf1(...): ... async d
